ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r1.claim: This surah pairs with Qiyamah and its first three verses dovetail with that surah's last four; both establish Judgment, though with different arguments.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r1.anchor: one will realize that they dovetail into one another

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r2.claim: Qiyamah argues from the inward reproaching soul, whereas this surah argues from human creation and the need to reward gratitude and punish ingratitude.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r2.anchor: the chiding soul present within man

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r3.speaker: some maṣāḥif
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r3.claim: Some muṣḥafs classify the surah as Medinan.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r3.anchor: In some ma ṣāḥif , this sūrah is regarded

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r4.claim: Islahi rejects a Medinan classification for every verse, saying subject matter is the criterion and this surah's subject confirms it is wholly Meccan.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r4.anchor: not even one verse of this sūrah was revealed

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r5.claim: For a time man was nonexistent; God created him from a drop through stages into a hearing, understanding being, endowed with awareness of good and evil and tested for gratitude.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r5.anchor: for a certain period of time he was a non-entity

QUSHAYRI:v3p373/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p373/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p373/r8.claim: God makes the paths of good and evil known; the person is either grateful or ungrateful.
QUSHAYRI:v3p373/r8.anchor: أي : عرفناه الطريق ؛ أي طريق الخير والشر

QUSHAYRI:v3p373/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p373/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p373/r9.claim: Another explanation reads the alternatives as bliss or misery, or as gratitude from God's friends through enabling grace versus disbelief from His enemies through abandonment.
QUSHAYRI:v3p373/r9.anchor: وقيل : إما للشقاوة ، وإما للسعادة ، إما شاكرا من أوليائنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r1.claim: God guided humanity by showing the road and the outcomes of guidance and destruction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r1.anchor: أخبر تعالى أنه هداه إلى السبيل، أي أرشده إلى الطريق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r2.speaker: مجاهد والسدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r2.claim: Mujahid says the path is the way to felicity or misery; al-Suddi says it is the route out of the womb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r2.anchor: وقال مجاهد: سبيل السعادة والشقاوة. وقال السدي: سبيل الخروج من الرحم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says God enabled both possibilities and invited people to Islam through rational and transmitted proofs, so belief or unbelief establishes responsibility.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r3.anchor: أي مكناه وأقدرناه في حالتيه جميعا، وإذ دعوناه إلى الإسلام بأدلة العقل والسمع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r4.speaker: أبو السمال وأبو العاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r4.claim: While most read imma with kasra, Abu al-Sammal and Abu al-ʿAj open both instances, a dialect reported by Abu Zayd and also used as a coordinating particle.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r4.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: إما بكسر الهمزة فيهما وأبو السمال وأبو العاج

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says gratitude comes by God’s enabling, while ingratitude comes from bad choice.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r5.anchor: والمعنى: إما شاكرا بتوفيقنا، وإما كفورا فبسوء اختياره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r6.claim: Shakiran and kafuran are circumstantial phrases from the object pronoun in ‘We guided him’; an alternative makes them describe the two paths metaphorically.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r6.anchor: وانتصب شاكرا وكفورا على الحال من ضمير النصب في هديناه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari also allows the adjectives to qualify the two paths, metaphorically describing them as grateful or ungrateful.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يكونا حالين من السبيل، أي عرفناه السبيل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r8.claim: Shakir is not intensified because gratitude is rare, while kafur is intensified because unbelief is common.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r8.anchor: كان الشكر قل من يتصف به قال شاكرا

FARRA:v3p213#2/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p213#2/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p213#2/r5.claim: Guiding someone to the path may take ila, li, or no preposition; hidaya means making the path known, whether the person gives thanks or rejects it.
FARRA:v3p213#2/r5.anchor: وإلى السبيل، وللسبيل. كل ذلك جائز في كلام العرب. يقول: هديناه: عرفناه السبيل،

FARRA:v3p213#2/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p213#2/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p213#2/r6.claim: Imma can introduce a conditional choice between gratitude and disbelief, or a paired alternative like punishment and repentance; the latter implies that God created the person wretched or fortunate.
FARRA:v3p213#2/r6.anchor: و (إما) هاهنا تكون جزاء، أي: إن شكر وإن كفر،

NAHHAS:v5p95/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p95/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p95/r7.claim: Shākiran and kafūran are circumstantial accusatives: the human is grateful or ungrateful; immā introduces the distinction.
NAHHAS:v5p95/r7.anchor: منصوبان على الحال أي إنا خلقنا الإنسان شاكرا أو كفورا ومعنى إما أو

NAHHAS:v5p95/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p95/r8.speaker: أهل التفسير
NAHHAS:v5p95/r8.claim: Exegetes say God guided the way, then one is wretched or blessed while in the womb, as the Prophet related; the states may be prospective.
NAHHAS:v5p95/r8.anchor: قول أهل التفسير أن المعنى إنا هديناه السبيل إما شقيا وإما سعيدا

NAHHAS:v5p95/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p95/r9.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v5p95/r9.claim: Al-Farrāʾ allows mā to be extra and inna conditional: 'if grateful or ungrateful.'
NAHHAS:v5p95/r9.anchor: وأجاز الفراء أن يكون ما ههنا زائدة وتكون أن للشرط والمجازاة

NAHHAS:v5p95/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p95/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p95/r10.claim: Abu Jaʿfar calls this plainly wrong: conditional inna cannot govern nouns, and the verse uses shākiran/kafūran rather than verbs.
NAHHAS:v5p95/r10.anchor: قال أبو جعفر وهذا القول ظاهره خطأ لأن أن التي للشرط لا تقع على الأسماء

BIQAI-FULL:v8p260/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p260/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p260/r1.claim: Biqāʿī places the passage after the deniers’ prideful rejection of resurrection, contrasting that posture with reflection on humanity’s humble origin.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p260/r1.anchor: ولما تقدم في القيامة إخباره تعالى عن حال منكري البعث عنادا واستكبارا وتعاميا عن النظر والاعتبار

BIQAI-FULL:v8p261/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p261/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p261/r1.claim: The Creator formed varied bones, joints, tendons, and ligaments, specifying their shapes and counts so the body can move and remain sound.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p261/r1.anchor: وقدرها بمقادير وأشكال مختلفة , فمنها صغير وكبير

BIQAI-FULL:v8p261/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p261/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p261/r2.claim: Distinct senses and organs serve precise purposes: eyes convey images, ears gather sound, the nose detects scents, teeth divide food, and the tongue expresses thought.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p261/r2.anchor: ففتح العين ورتب طبقاتها وأحسن شكلها ولونها وأحكمها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p261/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p261/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p261/r3.claim: Internal organs divide the work of digestion and circulation; the entire intricate body begins as a tiny drop in three layers of darkness, proving its unseen Maker.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p261/r3.anchor: وكان مبدأ ذلك كله النطفة على صغرها في داخل الرحمن في ظلمات ثلاثة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p261/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p261/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p261/r4.claim: People marvel at a fine design on a wall yet overlook the Creator of the far greater wonders in themselves and others.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p261/r4.anchor: فسبحانه ما أعظم شأنه وأبهر برهانه , فيالله العجب ممن يرى نقشا حسنا على جدار فيتعجب من حسنه

MUQATIL:76:1-3/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:76:1-3/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:76:1-3/r4.claim: God showed people both paths, misguidance and guidance.
MUQATIL:76:1-3/r4.anchor: { إنا هديناه السبيل } يعني سبيل الضلالة والهدى

MUQATIL:76:1-3/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:76:1-3/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:76:1-3/r5.claim: A thankful person is a monotheist who credits God with good creation; an ungrateful person denies God's oneness or assigns God's blessings to others.
MUQATIL:76:1-3/r5.anchor: { إما شاكرا } أن يكون { شاكرا } يعني موحدا

TABATABAI:76:1-22/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:76:1-22/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:76:1-22/r1.claim: Innate guidance is universal and equal because it belongs to human creation, but distractions and bad dispositions such as stubbornness can weaken its effect.
TABATABAI:76:1-22/r1.anchor: الهداية الفطرية عامة بالغة لا يستثنى منها إنسان لأنها لازم الخلقة الانسانية

TABATABAI:76:1-22/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:76:1-22/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:76:1-22/r2.claim: Inner guidance differs from religious, verbal guidance: the latter reaches society and can guide whoever prefers truth, but practical limits prevent it from reaching every person individually.
TABATABAI:76:1-22/r2.anchor: وأما الهداية القولية وهي التي تتضمنها الدعوة الدينية فإن من شأنها أن تبلغ المجتمع

TABATABAI:76:1-22/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:76:1-22/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:76:1-22/r3.claim: When the religious call reaches someone and truth becomes clear, the proof is established; one not reached clearly is treated with divine grace as vulnerable and left to God's judgment.
TABATABAI:76:1-22/r3.anchor: فمن بلغته الدعوة وانكشف له الحق فقد تمت عليه الحجة ومن لم تبلغه الدعوة بلوغا ينكشف به الحق

TABATABAI:76:1-22/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:76:1-22/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:76:1-22/r4.claim: The author distinguishes universal warning to every community from a particular warning to a people whose ancestors were not warned.
TABATABAI:76:1-22/r4.anchor: وإلى المعنى الأول أشار تعالى بقوله وإن من أمة إلا خلا فيها نذير

TABATABAI:76:1-22#6/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:76:1-22#6/r10.speaker: حمران بن أعين
TABATABAI:76:1-22#6/r10.claim: Al-Sadiq explains that taking the guided path makes one grateful, while leaving it makes one an unbeliever; Qummi and Tawhid reports give similar wording.
TABATABAI:76:1-22#6/r10.anchor: عن حمران بن أعين قال سألت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام عن قوله عز وجل { إنا هديناه السبيل إما شاكرا وإما كفورا } قال إما آخذ فهو شاكر وإما تارك

TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r16.claim: God made the path clear and supplied evidence for truth and falsehood so people could recognize them.
TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r16.anchor: أي بينا له الطريق ونصبنا له الأدلة وأزحنا له العلة حتى يتمكن

TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r17.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r17.claim: Qatada interprets the path as the routes of good and evil.
TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r17.anchor: وقيل: هو طريق الخير والشر عن قتادة

TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r18.claim: The path can mean knowledge of religion through reason and revelation, which every accountable person must follow to attain eternal reward.
TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r18.anchor: السبيل هو طريق معرفة الدين به يتوصل إلى ثواب الأبد ويلزم كل مكلف سلوكه

THALABI:v10p94/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p94/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p94/r8.claim: Nabtali means testing through commands and prohibitions; grammarians who see fronting and delay put the testing after making the person hearing and seeing.
THALABI:v10p94/r8.anchor: نبتليه نختبره بالأمر والنهي وقال بعض أهل العربية: هي مقدمة معناها التأخير

THALABI:v10p94/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p94/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p94/r9.claim: God clarifies the paths of truth and falsehood, guidance and error, and good and evil, as in the verse about the two high roads.
THALABI:v10p94/r9.anchor: إنا هديناه السبيل أي بينا له سبيل الحق والباطل والهدى والضلالة وعرفناه طريق الخير والشر

THALABI:v10p94/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p94/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p94/r10.claim: Shakir and kafur describe the person as either a believing, fortunate servant or a disbelieving, wretched one; another parse makes them the consequences of the clarified path, which al-Farra prefers.
THALABI:v10p94/r10.anchor: إما مؤمنا سعيدا وأما كافرا شقيا يعني خلقناه أما كذا وأما كذا، وقيل معنى الكلام: الجزاء

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:76:1-3/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:76:1-3/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:76:1-3/r3.claim: God clarified the path, making the person grateful or ungrateful; sending messengers made the proof clear whether one believes or disbelieves.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:76:1-3/r3.anchor: { إنا هديناه السبيل } بينا له الطريق { إما شاكرا وإما كفورا }

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p359/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p359/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p359/r2.claim: The opening contrasts the grateful and ungrateful; the ending contrasts those shown mercy with those punished.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p359/r2.anchor: في أول السورة ذكر الشاكر والكفور وفي خاتمتها ذكر المرحوم

ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r32.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r32.speaker: author
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r32.claim: The guided path is true Islam, leading directly to God and His pure blessings; it is the path described in 75:30, 75:12, and 53:42 and in the Opening chapter.
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r32.anchor: Kur’an ile davet olunan hak İslâm dinidir.

ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r33.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r33.speaker: author
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r33.claim: God sets revealed and created, transmitted and rational signs in the world and within people, and gives them hearing, sight, and insight to show their origin, destination, and duties.
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r33.anchor: tenzîlî ve tekvînî, naklî ve aklî âyetler, deliller, alâmetler nasb u ikāme ederek

ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r34.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r34.speaker: author
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r34.claim: Gratitude means recognizing guidance, believing with good intent, following the right path, enduring hardship, and moving toward perfection.
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r34.anchor: Rabbine şükretmek üzere iman ve hüsn-i niyetle o Hak yoluna sülûk edip mihnetlere göğüs gererek

ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r35.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r35.speaker: author
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r35.claim: Ingratitude means choosing disbelief, avoiding responsibility and moral growth, and acting as though one neither hears nor sees; guidance was shown in either case.
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r35.anchor: teklif ve tekemmülden kaçınarak, bu irşad ve hidâyete karşı, işitmez, görmezceden gelerek

ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r36.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r36.speaker: author
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r36.claim: The contrast encourages gratitude and warns against disbelief, offering a concise promise and threat like 41:40.
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r36.anchor: bir taraftan şükre tergīb, bir taraftan da küfürden tahzir için

BURSEVI:v10p201/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p201/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p201/r9.claim: Guidance follows the gift of senses and explains it: God showed the ways of good and evil, salvation and ruin, through revealed signs and proofs; it means direction, not guidance that necessarily brings attainment, as in 90:10.
BURSEVI:v10p201/r9.anchor: والمعنى أريناه وعرفناه طريق الخير والشر والنجاة والهلاك بإنزال الآيات ونصب الدلائل

BURSEVI:v10p201/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p201/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p201/r10.claim: Al-Irshad reads ‘whether grateful or ungrateful’ as two enabled states: the thankful person affirms divine benefaction and unity, while the ungrateful person denies it; gratitude acknowledges the benefactor and disbelief begins with denial.
BURSEVI:v10p201/r10.anchor: فالشاكر الموحد والكفور الجاحد لأن الشكر الإقرار بالنمعم ورأس الكفر إن جحوده

QASHANI:76:3-6/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:76:3-6/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:76:3-6/r1.claim: God guides by rational and transmitted proofs; grateful people use their faculties for obedience and reaching the Benefactor, while the ungrateful are veiled by blessings and misuse them.
QASHANI:76:3-6/r1.anchor: سبيل الحق بأدلة العقل والسمع في حالتي كونه شاكرا مهتديا مستعملا لنعم المشاعر

AKHFASH:v2p558/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p558/r5.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p558/r5.claim: إما شاكرا وإما كفورا has a parallel in إما العذاب وإما الساعة; one may omit إما conceptually and begin the following words independently in the nominative.
AKHFASH:v2p558/r5.anchor: وقال {إنا هديناه السبيل إما شاكرا وإما كفورا} كذلك {إما العذاب وإما الساعة} كأنك لم تذكر "إما" [180 ء] وان شئت ابتدأت ما بعدها فرفعته.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p374/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p374/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p374/r5.claim: The guidance clause explains testing and is arranged with stylistic variation; obligation reveals how people respond to a great charge.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p374/r5.anchor: وحقيقة الابتلاء : الاختبار لتعرف حال الشيء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p375/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p375/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p375/r3.claim: Being made subject to religious duties and law distinguishes humanity, grounds civilization, and leads into the statement that God guided the way.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p375/r3.anchor: وهذا تخلص إلى ما ميز الله به الإنسان من جعله تجاه التكليف واتباع الشرائع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p375/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p375/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p375/r4.claim: The guidance clause independently explains testing and elaborates the creation of hearing and sight, then turns from them to warning for disbelief and promise for gratitude.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p375/r4.anchor: استئناف بياني لبيان ما نشأ عن جملة { نبتليه }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p375/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p375/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p375/r5.claim: Guiding the way is an extended representation: God is guide, humanity the traveler, religious deeds the path, and success the destination.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p375/r5.anchor: فالله تعالى كالهادي ، والإنسان يشبه السائر المتحير في الطريق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p376/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p376/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p376/r1.claim: Taʾabbaṭa Sharran’s couplet shows that the nouns after both immā remain genitive through annexation and that the dual nūn is omitted.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p376/r1.anchor: فإن الاسمين بعد ( إما ) في الموضعين من البيت مجروران بالإضافة ولذلك حذفت النون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p376/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p376/r2.speaker: المرزوقي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p376/r2.claim: Al-Marzūqī explains the nominative reading as omitting the nūn because the phrase is lengthy, as though isār lengthened khuṭṭatā.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p376/r2.anchor: وزاد فقال ( وحذف النون إذا رفعت ( إسار ) استطالة للاسم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p376/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p376/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p376/r3.claim: Both “either” phrases are circumstantial predicates of the pronoun for the human; the two states accompany guidance after its delivery and reflection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p376/r3.anchor: و { إما شاكرا وإما كفورا } حالان من ضمير الغيبة في { هديناه }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p376/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p376/r4.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p376/r4.claim: Most grammarians treat immā as a simple particle of specification that neither governs the following noun nor blocks the preceding governor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p376/r4.anchor: و { إما } حرف تفصيل ، وهو حرف بسيط عند الجمهور

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p376/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p376/r5.speaker: سيبويه
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p376/r5.claim: Sibawayh analyzes immā as the conditional in plus negative mā, both stripped of their original functions to form a particle of specification.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p376/r5.anchor: وقال سيبويه : هو مركب من حرف ( إن ) الشرطية و ( ما ) النافية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p376/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p376/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p376/r6.claim: Some grammarians call the second immā a coordinator, but Ibn ʿĀshūr calls this arbitrary: the two immās are alike and waw is the actual coordinator, as poetry illustrates.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p376/r6.anchor: وقدّر بعض النحاة { إما } الثانية حرف عطف وهو تحكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p376/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p376/r7.speaker: ابن جني
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p376/r7.claim: Ibn Jinnī explains the genitive reading of “isār” in Taʾabbaṭa Sharran's couplet as deletion of the dual nun for annexation, since immā does not block annexation; the verse likewise omits the nun.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p376/r7.anchor: قال ابن جني : ( أما من جر ( إسار ) فإنه حذف النون للإضافة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p376/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p376/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p376/r8.claim: A person follows one of the two states after receiving and considering guidance: gratitude accepts it; ingratitude turns away, as a traveler could ignore directions and enter danger.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p376/r8.anchor: فإن أخذ بالهدى كان شاكرا وإن أعرض كان كفورا كمن لم يأخذ بإرشاد من يهديه الطريق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p377/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p377/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p377/r1.claim: The verse moves on to the recompense of the grateful and ungrateful, beginning with the unbelievers because their mention is nearer; emphatic warning signals a threat without leniency.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p377/r1.anchor: وأكد الخبر عن الوعيد بحرف التأكيد لإدخال الروع عليهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r9.claim: Guiding to the path may mean showing the general route to believer and unbeliever through senses, innate endowment, and signs of the Creator.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r9.anchor: يحتمل أن يريد السبيل العامة للمؤمن والكافر فذلك يختلق الحواس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r10.claim: Alternatively, God shows each person the path of his kind, believer toward faith and unbeliever toward disbelief; هديناه means showed rather than created faith.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r10.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد السبيل اسم الجنس، أي هدى المؤمن لإيمانه والكافر لكفره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r11.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r11.claim: Abu ʿAmr al-Dani parses شاكرا and كفورا as two circumstantial expressions in the إما division.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r11.anchor: وقوله تعالى: إما شاكرا وإما كفورا. حالان وقسمتهما إما، قاله أبو عمرو الداني،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r12.speaker: أبو العاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r12.claim: Abu al-ʿAj is cited for the reading إما شاكرا وإما كفورا; the author identifies him as Kathir ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Sulami, a Syrian governor in Basra.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r12.anchor: وقرأ أبو العاج «إما شاكرا وإما كفورا» وأبو العاج كثير بن عبد الله السلمي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p428#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p428#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p428#2/r1.claim: God made the path of guidance clear through proofs and by sending a messenger.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p428#2/r1.anchor: أي بينا له سبيل الهدى بنصب الأدلة وبعث الرسول

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p428#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p428#2/r2.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p428#2/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains that God made the path clear, whether the person is grateful or unbelieving.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p428#2/r2.anchor: قال الفراء بينا له الطريق إن شكر أو كفر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r1.claim: God clarified the paths of good and evil, like guiding Thamud and showing the two paths.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r1.anchor: بينا له طريق الخير وطريق الشر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r2.speaker: عكرمة وعطية وابن زيد ومجاهد والجمهور
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r2.claim: The well-known majority interpretation is that God made the way clear; Ibn Kathir calls this the correct view.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r2.anchor: وهذا قول عكرمة، وعطية، وابن زيد، ومجاهد -في المشهور عنه-والجمهور

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r3.speaker: مجاهد وأبو صالح والضحاك والسدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r3.claim: An unusual alternative takes guidance as emergence from the womb; Ibn Kathir rejects it in favor of the popular interpretation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r3.anchor: وهذا قول غريب، والصحيح المشهور الأول

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r4.claim: ‘Grateful or ungrateful’ is an accusative circumstantial phrase describing the person guided, meaning ultimately happy or wretched.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r4.anchor: منصوب على الحال من "الهاء" في قوله: {إنا هديناه السبيل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r5.speaker: أبو مالك الأشعري عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r5.claim: Everyone begins the day either ruining or freeing himself; Muslim transmits the report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r5.anchor: كل الناس يغدو، فبائع نفسه فموبقها أو معتقها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r6.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r6.claim: Every newborn is on the innate disposition until speech develops, then is grateful or ungrateful; Ibn Kathir links this to the verse on primordial nature.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r6.anchor: كل مولود يولد على الفطرة حتى يعرب عنه لسانه، فإذا أعرب عنه لسانه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r7.claim: Each person leaving home is followed by an angel’s or Satan’s banner, depending on whether the purpose pleases or angers God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r7.anchor: ما من خارج يخرج إلا ببابه رايتان: راية بيد ملك، وراية بيد شيطان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r8.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r8.claim: The Prophet warns Ka'b ibn Ujra about misguided rulers: endorsing their lies or assisting oppression disowns a person, while refusing both keeps him with the Prophet and his Pond.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r8.anchor: أمراء يكونون من بعدي، لا يهتدون بهداي، ولا يستنون بسنتي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r9.claim: The same report calls fasting a shield, charity an eraser of sin, prayer a قربان or proof, and warns that flesh nourished by illicit earnings belongs in Hell.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r9.anchor: الصوم جنة، والصدقة تطفئ الخطيئة، والصلاة قربان -أو قال: برهان

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r15.speaker: عطية
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r15.claim: He interprets the guided path as the paths of good and evil.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r16.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r16.claim: He reads it as guidance distinguishing right guidance from error.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r17.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r17.claim: He understands it as the path of misery and felicity.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r18.speaker: أبو صالح والضحاك والسدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r18.claim: They say it is the human's emergence from the womb.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r18.anchor: خروجه من الرحم , قاله أبو صالح والضحاك والسدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r19.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r19.claim: Other possibilities are the paths of benefit and harm that instinct reveals or the completion of intellect.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r19.anchor: سبيل منافعه ومضاره التي يهتدي إليها بطبعه , وقيل : كمال عقله

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r20.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r20.claim: He interprets thankful versus ungrateful as believer versus unbeliever.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r20.anchor: إما مؤمنا وإما كافرا , قاله يحيى بن سلام

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r21.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r21.claim: He interprets the pair as gratitude for blessing versus ingratitude toward it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r21.anchor: إما شكورا للنعمة وإما كفورا بها , قاله قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r22.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r22.claim: The wording intensifies ingratitude but not gratitude: gratitude to God cannot be fully achieved, whereas a person may be intensely ungrateful despite abundant blessings.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r22.anchor: نفيا للمبالغة في الشكر وإثباتا لها في الكفر , لأن شكر الله تعالى لا يؤدى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p302#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p302#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p302#4/r1.claim: God showed the path of guidance through rational proofs and revealed evidence.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p302#4/r1.anchor: بينا له طريق الهدى بأدلة العقل والسمع

NASAFI-FULL:v4p302#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p302#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p302#4/r2.claim: Thankful means believing and ungrateful means disbelieving; these may be circumstantial descriptions of the person guided.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p302#4/r2.anchor: ﴿ إما شاكرا ﴾ ا مؤمنا ﴿ وإما كفورا ﴾ كافرا حالان من الهاء في هديناه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p302#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p302#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p302#4/r3.claim: Alternatively, the path itself is figuratively described as a thankful path or an ungrateful path.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p302#4/r3.anchor: أو من السبيل أي عرفناه السبيل اما سبيلا شاكرا واما سبيلا كفورا ووصف السبيل بالشكر والكفر مجاز

NASAFI-FULL:v4p302#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p302#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p302#4/r4.claim: After naming the two groups, the text follows with what God prepared for each.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p302#4/r4.anchor: ولما ذكر الفريقين اتبعهما ما اعد لهما

QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r11.claim: God showed humanity guidance and error through messengers, as also said at 90:10.
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r11.anchor: أي بينا له وعرفناه طريق الهدى والضلال، والخير والشر ببعث الرسل

QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r12.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r12.claim: Mujahid says the path is the way to misery or felicity.
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r12.anchor: وقال مجاهد: أي بينا له السبيل إلى الشقاء والسعادة.

QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r13.speaker: الضحاك وأبو صالح والسدي
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r13.claim: Al-Dahhak, Abu Salih, and al-Suddi interpret the path as a person's exit from the womb.
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r13.anchor: وقال الضحاك وأبو صالح والسدي: السبيل هنا خروجه من الرحم.

QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r14.claim: Another view takes the path as benefits and harms recognized through instinct and developed reason.
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r14.anchor: وقيل: منافعه ومضاره التي يهتدي إليها بطبعه وكمال عقله.

QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r15.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r15.claim: The Kufans take in as a conditional particle with redundant ma, a reading al-Farra prefers; Basrans object that a noun needs an implied verb.
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r15.anchor: قال الكوفيون: «إن» ها هنا تكون جزاء و «ما» زائدة

QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r16.claim: Another explanation says God showed proofs of monotheism; faith follows if He creates guidance, and unbelief if He abandons a person.
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r16.anchor: وقيل: أي هديناه الرشد، أي بينا له سبيل التوحيد بنصب الأدلة عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r17.speaker: الماوردي
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r17.claim: Al-Mawardi explains the word choice: human gratitude is not intensive because God's favors cannot be repaid, while human disbelief is abundant.

SAMIN-DURR:76:3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:76:3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:76:3/r1.claim: شاكرًا is an accusative circumstantial phrase qualifying the object of هديناه, meaning He showed the person both possible states; Abu al-Baqa allows a prospective state.
SAMIN-DURR:76:3/r1.anchor: شاكرا " نصب على الحال، وفيه وجهان، أحدهما: أنه حال من مفعول " هديناه " ، أي: هديناه مبينا له كلتا حالتيه

SAMIN-DURR:76:3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:76:3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:76:3/r2.claim: Alternatively the circumstantial phrase qualifies السبيل metaphorically, as in هديناه النجدين; the path is called grateful or ungrateful.
SAMIN-DURR:76:3/r2.anchor: والثاني: أنه حال من " السبيل " على المجاز. قال الزمخشري: " ويجوز أن يكونا حالين من " السبيل

SAMIN-DURR:76:3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:76:3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:76:3/r3.claim: The common kasra reading of إما makes it synonymous with أو; grammarians have previously differed on its analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:76:3/r3.anchor: والعامة على كسر همزة " إما " وهي المرادفة ل " أو " وتقدم خلاف النحويين فيها

SAMIN-DURR:76:3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:76:3/r4.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:76:3/r4.claim: He transmits the Kufan view that إما is conditional إن plus ما, but Basrans reject it because إن does not govern nouns without an implied verb.
SAMIN-DURR:76:3/r4.anchor: ونقل مكي عن الكوفيين أنها هنا " إن " الشرطية زيدت بعدها " ما " ثم قال: " وهذا لا يجيزه البصريون

SAMIN-DURR:76:3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:76:3/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:76:3/r5.claim: The author rejects the objection that an implied verb would force شاكرًا into nominative; one can supply a verb governing it in the accusative.
SAMIN-DURR:76:3/r5.anchor: قلت: لا نسلم أنه يلزم رفع " شاكرا " مع إضمار الفعل، ويمكن أن يضمر فعل ينصب " شاكرا

SAMIN-DURR:76:3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:76:3/r6.speaker: أبو السمال وأبو العجاج
SAMIN-DURR:76:3/r6.claim: They read إما with fatḥa; it can be the coordinating conjunction in a dialect, as attested by poetry, or the detailed أما construction with an omitted response.
SAMIN-DURR:76:3/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو السمال وأبو العجاج بفتحها. وفيها وجهان، أحدهما: أنها العاطفة

SAMIN-DURR:76:3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:76:3/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:76:3/r7.claim: For the detailed reading, he supplies an omitted contrast: gratitude comes through divine enabling, while disbelief comes from the person's bad choice.
SAMIN-DURR:76:3/r7.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " وهي قراءة حسنة والمعنى: أما شاكرا فبتوفيقنا، وأما كفورا فبسوء اختياره

RAZI-FULL:v30p210#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p210#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p210#2/r1.claim: After forming the human and giving outward and inward faculties, God made the paths of guidance and error clear.
RAZI-FULL:v30p210#2/r1.anchor: أنه بعد أن ركبه وأعطاه الحواس الظاهرة والباطنة بين له سبيل الهدى والضلال

RAZI-FULL:v30p210#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p210#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p210#2/r2.claim: The senses precede intellect in existence: perception yields basic judgments such as non-contradiction and the whole being greater than its part, which reasoning then uses to reach unknown conclusions.
RAZI-FULL:v30p210#2/r2.anchor: إذا أحس بالمحسوسات تنبه لمشاركات بينها ومباينات ، ينتزع منها عقائد صادقة أولية

RAZI-FULL:v30p210#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p210#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p210#2/r3.claim: If hearing and sight mean intellect, the first verse says intellect was given so that the path and what must or must not be done could be known.
RAZI-FULL:v30p210#2/r3.anchor: ومن قال : المراد من كونه سميعا بصيرا هو العقل ، قال : إنه لما بين في الآية الأولى

RAZI-FULL:v30p210#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p210#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p210#2/r4.claim: Sabīl may mean the routes of good and evil, salvation and ruin; the singular is generic, and God has identified and explained both.

RAZI-FULL:v30p210#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p210#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p210#2/r5.claim: Alternatively, sabīl means only the path of guidance, the path deserving that name absolutely; a path of error is named only relationally.
RAZI-FULL:v30p210#2/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المراد بالسبيل ، هو سبيل الهدى لأنها هي الطريقة المعروفة المستحقة لهذا الاسم

RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r1.claim: Guiding to the path means creating signs, guiding intellect, sending prophets, and revealing books; it does not mean creating actual guidance, but showing the route.
RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r1.anchor: المراد من هداية السبيل خلق الدلائل ، وخلق العقل الهادي وبعثة الأنبياء وإنزال الكتب

RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r2.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the verb may be used with “the path,” “to the path,” or “for the path.”
RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r2.anchor: قال الفراء : هديناه السبيل ، وإلى السبيل وللسبيل ، كل ذلك جائز

RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r3.claim: One parsing makes grateful and ungrateful circumstantial states of the human: God's direction is complete in either belief or disbelief.
RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r3.anchor: أن شاكر أو كفورا حالان من الهاء ، في هديناه السبيل

RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r4.claim: Another parsing supplies an omitted kāna: whether he was grateful or ungrateful.
RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r4.anchor: أنه انتصب قوله شاكرا وكفورا بإضمار كان

RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r5.claim: A third reads the guidance as enabling a distinction between gratitude and disbelief, obedience and sin, as in verses about testing people's deeds.
RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r5.anchor: معناه إنا هديناه السبيل ، ليكون إما شاكرا وإما كفورا أي ليتميز شكره من كفره

RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r6.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r6.claim: Al-Qaffāl compares the omitted conditional fa to saying, “I advised you; if you wish, accept, and if you wish, leave it.”
RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r6.anchor: قال القفال : ومجاز هذه الكلمة على هذا التأويل قول القائل ، قد نصحت لك

RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r7.claim: The wording may also be a warning: choose belief or disbelief, for God has prepared the fitting outcome for each.
RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r7.anchor: على جهة الوعيد أي إنا هديناه السبيل فإن شاء فليكفر وإن شاء فليشكر

RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r8.claim: A fourth parsing treats grateful and ungrateful as circumstantial descriptions of the path itself, a figurative attribution.
RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r8.anchor: أن يكونا حالين من السبيل أي عرفناه السبيل ، أي إما سبيلا شاكرا ، وإما سبيلا كفورا

STUDYQURAN:76:3/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:76:3/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:76:3/r1.claim: The verse parallels 90:8–10: God provides guidance, and people are accountable for their own souls.
STUDYQURAN:76:3/r1.anchor: Both passages indicate that God provides guidance for those who have eyes to see and ears to hear

STUDYQURAN:76:3/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:76:3/r2.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:76:3/r2.claim: God's guidance may come through human intellect.

STUDYQURAN:76:3/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:76:3/r3.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:76:3/r3.claim: God's guidance may come through the messengers He sends.

STUDYQURAN:76:3/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:76:3/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:76:3/r4.claim: Guidance may also come through signs in revelation, creation, and the human being.
STUDYQURAN:76:3/r4.anchor: the many signs in revelation, in the created order, and within the human being

STUDYQURAN:76:3/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:76:3/r5.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:76:3/r5.claim: Grateful and ungrateful may mean happy and wretched.
STUDYQURAN:76:3/r5.anchor: Grateful or ungrateful indicates being either happy or wretched (IK)

STUDYQURAN:76:3/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:76:3/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:76:3/r6.claim: The terms may also mean believer and disbeliever, as illustrated by 18:29.
STUDYQURAN:76:3/r6.anchor: or a believer or a disbeliever, as in 18:29

ZAJJAJ:v5p257#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p257#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p257#2/r1.claim: God guided the human being to the path, either toward wretchedness or toward happiness.
ZAJJAJ:v5p257#2/r1.anchor: معناه هديناه الطريق إما لشقوة وإما لسعادة

TABATABAI:76:2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:76:2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:76:2/r1.claim: The sura describes human creation and guidance to gratitude or disbelief, then punishment and the blessings of the righteous at length; it closes by telling the Prophet to remain patient and worship.
TABATABAI:76:2/r1.anchor: تذكر السورة خلق الإنسان بعد ما لم يكن شيئا مذكورا ثم هدايته السبيل إما شاكرا وإما كفورا وأن الله إعتد للكافرين أنواع العذاب

TABATABAI:76:2-3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:76:2-3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:76:2-3/r4.claim: Hearing and sight equip human beings to receive God's call through prophets and books and to see signs of the origin and return, guiding them to faith and good works or punishment.
TABATABAI:76:2-3/r4.anchor: جعله سميعا بصيرا للتوسل به في التدبير الربوبي إلى غايته وهي أن يرى آيات الله الدالة على المبدإ والمعاد ويسمع

TABATABAI:76:2-3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:76:2-3/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:76:2-3/r6.claim: Guidance here is showing the route, not delivering someone to the destination; the path is the true road that reaches its intended end.
TABATABAI:76:2-3/r6.anchor: الهداية بمعنى إراءة الطريق دون الإيصال إلى المطلوب والمراد بالسبيل السبيل بحقيقة معنى الكلمة وهو المؤدي إلى الغاية المطلوبة

TABATABAI:76:2-3/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:76:2-3/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:76:2-3/r7.claim: Gratitude means using a blessing while acknowledging its giver; ingratitude uses it while concealing that it came from the benefactor.
TABATABAI:76:2-3/r7.anchor: والشكر استعمال النعمة بإظهار كونها من منعمها وقد تقدم في تفسير قوله تعالى

TABATABAI:76:3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:76:3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:76:3/r1.claim: True gratitude means sincerity toward God; ingratitude uses His gift while hiding its source.
TABATABAI:76:3/r1.anchor: كون العبد شاكرا لله كونه مخلصا لربه، والكفران استعمالها مع ستر كونها من المنعم.

TABATABAI:76:3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:76:3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:76:3/r2.claim: The two states are circumstances of the guided person, not the path; imma divides humanity into grateful and ungrateful, each having been shown the way.
TABATABAI:76:3/r2.anchor: يفيد التقسيم والتنويع أي إنا هديناه السبيل حال كونه منقسما

TABATABAI:76:3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:76:3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:76:3/r3.claim: The path is the religious way of life leading to happiness and nearness to God, the true religion of Islam; interpreting it as the route out of the womb is unsound.
TABATABAI:76:3/r3.anchor: هو الدليل أولا على أن المراد بالسبيل السنة والطريقة التي يجب على الإنسان أن يسلكها في حياته الدنيا

TABATABAI:76:3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:76:3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:76:3/r4.claim: The path is chosen freely: gratitude and disbelief are within human choice, without coercion; God's will concerns the person's willing rather than negating the effect of that will on action.
TABATABAI:76:3/r4.anchor: وثانيا أن السبيل المهدي إليه سبيل اختياري وأن الشكر والكفر اللذين يترتبان على الهداية المذكورة واقعان في مستقر الاختيار للإنسان أن يتلبس بأيهما شاء

TABATABAI:76:3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:76:3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:76:3/r5.claim: Divine guidance includes innate prompting through human nature toward true belief and good action, as well as spoken guidance through prophets, messengers, revealed books, and revealed laws.
TABATABAI:76:3/r5.anchor: والهداية التي هي نوع إيذان واعلام منه تعالى للإنسان هداية فطرية هي تنبيه بسبب نوع خلقته وما جهز به وجوده

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God made the paths of guidance clear to the human being.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says both هديناه السبيل and هديناه إلى السبيل are valid, meaning that God made the way known.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16/r2.anchor: الفراء: هديناه السبيل، وإلى السبيل، كل ذلك جائز، يقول عرفناه السبيل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās begins to interpret grateful and ungrateful as monotheist and obedient or polytheist; the explanation continues in the following segment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد إما موحدا طائعا لله، و (إما) مشركا بالله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās completes his gloss by saying the alternatives occur in God’s knowledge.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says imā may function conditionally: if they are grateful or if they disbelieve.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r2.anchor: قال الفراء: و (إما) هاهنا تكون جزاء، أي إن شكروا (¬5) أو كفروا (¬6)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r3.claim: God clarifies the path of monotheism by evidence and messengers: a person may believe gratefully or reject it in disbelief.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r3.anchor: بين سبيل التوحيد، ودل عليه بنصب الأدلة، وبعث الرسل، شكر الإنسان فآمن, أو كفر فجحد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r4.claim: Guidance here means showing the way, not creating guidance in a person; once the path is shown, a person may be enabled to follow and believe or abandoned and disbelieve.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r4.anchor: ومعنى: (هدينا) هاهنا: بينا , وليس معناه خلقنا الهداية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r5.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r5.claim: Muqātil takes the path as both guidance and misguidance, leaving a person either monotheistic or unbelieving after the way is shown.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r5.anchor: قال مقاتل: يعني بينا له سبيل الهدى، وسبيل الضلالة، إما أن يكون موحدا فيما بين له، أو كافرا فلا يوحده

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r6.claim: Mujāhid interprets the path as misery and happiness, that is, the routes of truth and falsehood or good and evil.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r6.anchor: مجاهد: (إنا هديناه السبيل) قال: الشقاء والسعادة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r7.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r7.claim: Al-Farrāʾ also compares imā to the alternative in the verse about whether God punishes or pardons them, yielding the meaning that He created the person wretched or happy.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r7.anchor: قال الفراء: و (إما) (أن) (¬4) تكون على: (إما) التي في قوله: {إما يعذبهم} (¬5) فكأنه قال: خلقناه شقيا، أو سعيدا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r8.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r8.claim: Al-Zajjāj says God showed the way as either misery or happiness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r8.anchor: الزجاج: معناه: هديناه الطريق إما الشقوة، وإما السعادة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r9.claim: He calls the verse an argument against the Qadariyya because God says He guided people to the paths of happiness and misery.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r9.anchor: والآية حجة على القدرية (¬2)؛ لأن الله تعالى ذكر أنه هدى الإنسان (إلى) (¬3) طرق السعادة، والشقاوة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r10.claim: On one grammatical analysis, grateful or ungrateful is an accusative with an understood if-be clause or with an understood God-made-him clause; al-Akhfash also allows construing the terms adverbially with the path.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r10.anchor: وانتصب شاكرا أو كفورا على القول الأول بإضمار على التقدير (¬4): إما (كان) (¬5) شاكرا، وإما جعلناه (¬6) كفورا

ASAD-NOTES:76:3/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:76:3/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:76:3/r1.claim: God has shown humanity the way, leaving each person to prove grateful or ungrateful.
ASAD-NOTES:76:3/r1.anchor: Verily, We have shown him the way: [4] [and it rests with him to prove himself] either grateful or ungrateful.

ASAD-NOTES:76:3#n4/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:76:3#n4/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:76:3#n4/r1.claim: Hearing and sight signify reason and instinctive moral discernment; God also guides people through revelation given to prophets.
ASAD-NOTES:76:3#n4/r1.anchor: with "hearing and sight", i.e., with reason and the instinctive ability to discern between right and wrong, good and evil

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:3/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:3/r1.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:3/r1.claim: One interpretation is that God explained the paths of guidance and error, good and evil, as also stated in Beled 90:10.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:3/r1.anchor: Biz insana hidâyet ve dalâlet, hayır ve şer yollarını açıklayarak gideceği yolu gösterdik

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:3/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:3/r2.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:3/r2.claim: Another interpretation is that God explained the paths of happiness and misery.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:3/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:3/r3.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:3/r3.claim: A third interpretation is that God created people with the capacity to understand their profit and loss.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:3/r3.anchor: Kâr ve zararını anlayacak yetenekte yarattık

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:3/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:3/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:3/r4.claim: God created people rational, free, and able to distinguish good from evil; through prophets and revelation He showed the right way and gave them choice, so gratitude or ingratitude depends on how they use their capacities.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:3/r4.anchor: Allah Teâlâ insanı akıllı, iradeli ve iyiyi kötüden ayırma kabiliyetine sahip değerli bir varlık olarak yaratmış; görevlendirdiği peygamberler ve indirdiği vahiyle ona doğru yolu göstermiş

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p303/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p303/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p303/r2.claim: Human names hearing, sight, and guidance as means of testing, so نبتليه fits its fuller account; al-Mulk omits those means and moves to the heavens, suiting يبلوكم.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p303/r2.anchor: فلما أطال في ذكر ما تردد أطال في صيغة الإبتلاء

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p306/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p306/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p306/r2.claim: The passage names every condition of testing: God and the human, hearing, sight, reason, choice and its paths, the two responses, and their outcomes in Paradise or Hell.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p306/r2.anchor: لم يدع شيئاً يخص الابتلاء إلا وذكره في هذه الآية

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p307/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p307/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p307/r1.claim: Hearing and sight precede guidance because they convey information to the mind and usually enable understanding of guidance and rulings.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p307/r1.anchor: السمع والبصر يوصلان المعلومات إلى العقل وبدونهما تتعسّر الهداية

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p309/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p309/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p309/r1.claim: إنا هديناه echoes إنا خلقنا with emphatic divine attribution because guidance is crucial, perhaps exceeding creation; if creation for worship is emphasized, guidance must be emphasized too.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p309/r1.anchor: إذا كان الخلق مؤكد فلا بد من أن تكون الهداية مؤكدة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p309/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p309/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p309/r2.claim: Only God can provide the sound way; human reasoning left unaided would divide people into factions, while the Creator knows what benefits them.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p309/r2.anchor: المنهج الصحيح لا يستطيعه أحد إلا الله تعالى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p310/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p310/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p310/r1.claim: هدى can take no preposition for someone already on the path, إلى for directing someone toward it, or ل for showing its features; using it directly here encompasses both bringing the distant person to the path and explaining it once reached, completing God's guidance and warranting thanks.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p310/r1.anchor: عدم تعدية الفعل في الآية بحرف جر جمعت المعنيين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p311/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p311/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p311/r1.claim: The verse pairs the ordinary active participle شاكراً with intensive كفوراً: using شكور would exclude the many who are grateful but not exceptionally so, while كافر is Quranically paired with believer rather than grateful.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p311/r1.anchor: لم يقل إما شاكراً وإما كافراً أو إما شكوراً وإما كفورا

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p311/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p311/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p311/r2.claim: كفور can mean an intense disbeliever or one who denies blessings; here it means ingrate, as in كان الشيطان لربه كفورا.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p311/r2.anchor: صيغة كفور يستعملها القرآن لأمرين: للكافر المبالغ في الكفر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p311/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p311/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p311/r3.claim: The ل in لربه is an emphatic strengthening particle, not the preposition for disbelief in God: disbelief takes ب, while denial of a blessing takes the object directly; strengthening ل can accompany an intensive form or delayed predicate.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p311/r3.anchor: اللام هنا هي لام التقوية إذا جئنا بصيغة المبالغة أو اسم الفاعل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p312/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p312/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p312/r1.claim: Human chooses gratitude rather than belief because creation, senses, reason, choice, and guidance are additional favors that call for gratitude beyond faith; al-Taghabun mentions creation alone and pairs disbeliever with believer.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p312/r1.anchor: كل هذه نعم تقتضي الشكر فهو الإيمان وزيادة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p313/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p313/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p313/r1.claim: The surah's emphasis on feeding for God's sake and on the servants' praised effort also makes gratitude central to its overall atmosphere.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p313/r1.anchor: فذكر الشكر مناسب من جهة السياق ومن ناحية جو السورة الكلي

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p313/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p313/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p313/r2.claim: The easy, traversable سبيل calls for gratitude, whereas the two difficult نجد paths require striving and patience, as the following passage says.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p313/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p313/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p313/r3.claim: The grateful are named first because prior blessings call for thanks and the surah spends seventeen verses on their reward, while it summarizes punishment in one verse.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p313/r3.anchor: الإفاضة في ذكر جزاء الجنة وذكر الشاكرين اقتضى تقديم الشاكرين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p314/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p314/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p314/r1.claim: Gratitude comes before ingratitude because the surah begins and ends with mercy before punishment, maintaining the same order throughout.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p314/r1.anchor: فأول السورة وآخرها على نفس النسق

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p314/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p314/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p314/r2.claim: The Quran usually mentions gratitude before disbelief; al-Zumar reverses the order because its context foregrounds deniers and describes their punishment before the reward of the God-fearing.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p314/r2.anchor: والسبب في ذلك أنه تقدم ذكر الكفر والكافرين في سورة الزمر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p316/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p316/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p316/r3.claim: The punishment is said to be for الكافرين rather than الكفور: naming all disbelievers prevents implying ordinary disbelievers escape, while the more intensely unbelieving deserve still greater punishment.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p316/r3.anchor: لو قال أعتدنا للكُفُر لكان يذهب الظن أن العذاب يتناول المبالغ في الكفر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p317/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p317/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p317/r1.claim: Because God gave people freedom to choose in life, those who chose wrongly are bound in the afterlife; chains restrain legs and fetters restrain necks and hands.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p317/r1.anchor: فكما أساء الاختيار في الدنيا قيّده بالسلاسل

ALUSI-FULL:v29p153/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p153/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p153/r1.claim: The independent explanatory clause says God showed the path through revealed evidence and rational signs in the world and within the self, after accountability and testing.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p153/r1.anchor: أي دللناه على ما يوصله من الدلائل السمعية كالآيات التنزيلية والعقلية كالآيات الآفاقية والأنفسية

ALUSI-FULL:v29p153/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p153/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p153/r2.claim: “Thankful or ungrateful” may describe two states of the same person, since the path is shown in either state, or divide people: some follow truth gratefully and others reject it arrogantly.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p153/r2.anchor: إما للتفصيل باعتبار تعدد الأحوال مع اتحاد الذات أي هديناه ودللناه على ما يوصل إلى البغية

ALUSI-FULL:v29p153/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p153/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p153/r3.claim: A further grammatical possibility describes the two paths themselves as thankful and ungrateful by metonymy for their walkers.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p153/r3.anchor: حالان من السبيل أي عرفناه السبيل إما سبيلا شاكرا وإما سبيلا كفورا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p153/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p153/r4.speaker: السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p153/r4.claim: Al-Suddi says “the path” means the route by which an infant exits the womb; Alusi rejects this as wholly untenable.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p153/r4.anchor: وعن السدي أن السبيل هنا سبيل الخروج من الرحم وليس بشيء أصلا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p153/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p153/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p153/r5.claim: Abu al-Sammal and Abu al-Ajjaj read imma with an open initial vowel both times, a dialect form that some classify among conjunctions; a cited line of poetry attests the paired form.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p153/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو السمال وأبو العاج أما بفتح الهمزة في الموضعين وهي لغة حكاها أبو زيد

ALUSI-FULL:v29p153/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p153/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v29p153/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari construes the alternatives conditionally: gratitude comes by God's enabling, while disbelief comes from one's poor choice.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p153/r6.anchor: وجعلها الزمخشري أما التفصيلية المتضمنة معنى الشرط على معنى أما شاكرا فبتوفيقنا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p153/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p153/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p153/r7.claim: Alusi finds that conditional gloss strained and favors taking the alternatives as different responses to God's guidance, which can apply to either outcome without making guidance the opposite of misguidance.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p153/r7.anchor: وهذا التقدير إبراز من هلل ولا عليه أن يجعله من باب يضل به كثيرا ويهدي به كثيرا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p153/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p153/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p153/r8.claim: Another explanation makes the thankful person rewarded and the ungrateful punished; the emphatic form “ungrateful” also accommodates the rhyme and suggests ordinary people rarely escape some ingratitude.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p153/r8.anchor: وجوز الانتصاف أن يكون أما شاكرا فمثاب وأما كفورا فمعاقب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p292#3/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p292#3/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p292#3/r1.claim: God showed the human the path of truth and falsehood, guidance and misguidance, and good and evil.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p292#3/r1.anchor: {إنا هديناه السبيل} أي بينا له سبيل الحق والباطل والهدى والضلالة، وعرفناه طريق الخير والشر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p292#3/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p292#3/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p292#3/r2.claim: The person is either a grateful believer and fortunate or an ungrateful unbeliever and wretched.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p292#3/r2.anchor: {إما شاكرا وإما كفورا} إما مؤمنا سعيدا وإما كافرا شقيا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p292#3/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p292#3/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p292#3/r3.claim: Another interpretation reads the clause as a result: God made the path clear whether the person would be grateful or ungrateful.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p292#3/r3.anchor: وقيل: معنى الكلام الجزاء، يعني: بينا له الطريق إن شكر أو كفر

BAYDAWI-FULL:76:3-4/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:76:3-4/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:76:3-4/r1.claim: God showed humanity the path by setting out proofs and sending down signs.

BAYDAWI-FULL:76:3-4/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:76:3-4/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:76:3-4/r2.claim: Thankful and ungrateful are two states of the human referent: all are shown the path, then some follow it and some turn away; alternatively they qualify the path figuratively.
BAYDAWI-FULL:76:3-4/r2.anchor: أي { هدينه } في حاليه جميعا أو مقسوما إليهما بعضهم { شكرا }

BAYDAWI-FULL:76:3-4/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:76:3-4/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:76:3-4/r3.claim: A reading with fatḥ on ammā omits the response; ungrateful rather than unbelieving preserves the rhyme and signals widespread ingratitude, though culpability lies in deep indulgence.
BAYDAWI-FULL:76:3-4/r3.anchor: محافظة على الفواصل، وإشعارا بأن الإنسان لا يخلو عن كفران غالبا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p264/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p264/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p264/r2.claim: God guides by making the clear path known through revealed books, messengers, signs within and beyond the self, and insight that distinguishes truth from falsehood and divine speech from human speech.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p264/r2.anchor: بما أنزل من الكتب وأرسلنا من الرسل ونصبنا من الدلائل في الأنفس والآفاق

BIQAI-FULL:v8p264/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p264/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p264/r3.claim: The two human outcomes are thankfulness and ingratitude: shākir is an unmarked active participle because no one can fully thank every blessing, while kafūr is intensive because people can become deeply ungrateful, even by denying one favor.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p264/r3.anchor: معرفا له أنه لا يأخذه إلا بالتوغل فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p264/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p264/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p264/r4.claim: Thankfulness is named first as the human norm and because mercy precedes anger; ingratitude includes turning away, denial, worship of others, and stubbornness.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p264/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p264/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v8p264/r5.claim: The Prophet says every child is born upon the fiṭrah, after which parents make the child Jewish, Christian, or Magian; the author cites versions transmitted from Abū Hurayrah, Ibn ʿAbbās, Jābir, and al-Aswad ibn Surayʿ.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p264/r5.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( كل مولود يولد على الفطرة

DURR-FULL:v8p367/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r14.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r14.claim: Qatada traces development from drop through clot, lump, bone, flesh, and hair; God explains origins to test gratitude and knowledge of His rights, then guides people to gratitude or ingratitude.
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r14.anchor: عن قتادة {إنا خلقنا الإنسان من نطفة أمشاج نبتليه} قال: طورا نطفة وطورا علقة وطورا مضغة

DURR-FULL:v8p368/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p368/r3.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p368/r3.claim: 'We guided him to the way' means guidance to the path.
DURR-FULL:v8p368/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة {إنا هديناه السبيل} قال: السبيل الهدى

DURR-FULL:v8p368/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p368/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p368/r4.claim: The way comprises felicity and wretchedness.
DURR-FULL:v8p368/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد {إنا هديناه السبيل} قال: الشقاوة والسعادة

DURR-FULL:v8p368/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p368/r5.speaker: عطية العوفي
DURR-FULL:v8p368/r5.claim: The way is good and evil.
DURR-FULL:v8p368/r5.anchor: عن عطية العوفي {إنا هديناه السبيل} قال: الخير والشر

DURR-FULL:v8p368/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p368/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p368/r6.claim: Every child is born upon the natural disposition until able to speak; thereafter he is grateful or ungrateful.
DURR-FULL:v8p368/r6.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: كل مولد يولد على الفطرة حتى يعبر عنه لسانه

BURHAN:v4p244/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p244/r4.speaker: صاحب الأزهية
BURHAN:v4p244/r4.claim: The Azhiyya author says this use ordinarily repeats إما; repetition can be omitted when a substitute such as إلا occurs in the other clause.
BURHAN:v4p244/r4.anchor: حكمها في هذا القسم التكرير ولا تكرير اذا كان في الكلام عوض من تكريرها

BURHAN:v4p244/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p244/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p244/r5.claim: إما can express indeterminacy, as in whether God punishes or relents, and also occurs in nonrepeated conditional constructions built from إن plus redundant ما.
BURHAN:v4p244/r5.anchor: وتكون بمعنى الشرطية مركبة من إن الشرطية وما الزائدة وهذه لا تكرر

BURHAN:v4p244/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p244/r6.speaker: البصريون
BURHAN:v4p244/r6.claim: The Basrans read إما here as choice and parse شاكرا and كفورا as accusative circumstantial phrases.
BURHAN:v4p244/r6.anchor: فقال البصريون للتخيير فانتصاب شاكرا وكفورا على الحال

BURHAN:v4p244/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p244/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p244/r7.claim: Other analyses say the choice concerns God’s declaration that He does what He wills, or treat the states as signs: gratitude signals felicity and disbelief misery.
BURHAN:v4p244/r7.anchor: وقيل التخيير هنا راجع إلى اخبار الله بانه يفعل مايشاء وقيل حال مقيدة أي إما إن تجد عندهما الشكر فهو علامة السعادة أو الكفر فهو علامة الشقاوة

BURHAN:v4p244/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p244/r8.speaker: الكوفيون
BURHAN:v4p244/r8.claim: The Kufans allow a conditional reading, meaning whether the person is grateful or ungrateful; Makkī rejects it because a conditional إن does not govern a noun here without an omitted verb, which would wrongly make شاكر nominative.
BURHAN:v4p244/r8.anchor: واجاز الكوفيون إن تكون ها هنا شرطية أي إن شكر وإن كفر قال مكي وهذا ممنوع لان الشرطية لاتدخل على الاسماء إلا إن تضمر بعد إن فعلا

BURHAN:v2p513/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p513/r8.speaker: عبد الجبار بن أحمد
BURHAN:v2p513/r8.claim: Answering Sahib ibn Abbad, Abd al-Jabbar says each act of thanks is small against God's many gifts, while each act of ingratitude is great; hence شاكرا versus emphatic كفورا.
BURHAN:v2p513/r8.anchor: هذا سأله الصاحب بن عباد للقاضي عبد الجبار بن أحمد المعتزلي فأجاب بأن نعم الله على عباده كثيرة

ITQAN:v2p448#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p448#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p448#2/r1.claim: With kasra and shadda, إما has several grammatical functions.

ITQAN:v2p448#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p448#2/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p448#2/r4.claim: In 76:3, إما marks a division into the grateful and the ungrateful.
ITQAN:v2p448#2/r4.anchor: والتفصيل نحو ﴿ إما شاكرا وإما كفورا ﴾
